UN committee adopts draft resolutions on Palestinian aid, property rights and Israeli occupation
The United Nations General Assembly's Fourth Committee adopted on Wednesday three draft resolutions concerning support for the mandate and operations of the UN Agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA), the rights of Palestinian refugees to their properties, and the reaffirmation of the illegality of Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem and the Syrian Golan.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US sanctions Lebanese nationals, entities over Hezbollah links
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US sanctions Lebanese nationals, entities over Hezbollah links
The US Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on three Lebanese individuals and three entities, which it accuses of aiding Hezbollah, in its latest effort to destroy the group’s financial networks around the world.
In a statement, the department said it placed them on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, without specifying the charges or the evidence against them.
One of the organisations, "Wa Ta’awanu Association", was described as "a charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services".
"The US government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added in a post on X.
The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated. The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US judge rules in favour of foreign students and journalists after Trump limits visas
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US judge rules in favour of foreign students and journalists after Trump limits visas
A US federal judge has thrown out the Trump administration's attempt to limit visas for international students and members of the foreign press after university and media unions filed a lawsuit against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in August.
Massachusetts District Judge Dennis Saylor said on Monday that the government has been unable to prove there has been widespread visa fraud or national security concerns with this particular visa programme.
DHS's move to impose restrictions "is arbitrary and capricious", Saylor said in his decision.
"The Final Rule, entitled Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media... is hereby VACATED," he wrote.
Saylor added that DHS is "seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity - providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States - that Congress sought to permit and encourage".
The ruling preserves the "duration of status" or "D/S" stamp that international students receive on their visas and, by extension, on the visas foreign journalists receive as well.
It means they are legally permitted to stay in the country as long as they remain in the status they obtained, either as active students or working journalists, whether it's mere months or several years.

Israeli forces say ground operation in Gaza to dismantle Hamas tunnels
Israeli forces said on Wednesday that they launched a new military operation in Gaza to dismantle a tunnel west of the "Yellow Line".
The Israeli military said in a statement that the army and the internal security agency Shin Bet launched the joint operation to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".
The Yellow Line separates the Palestinian and Israeli-controlled areas in Gaza, with the Israeli army saying it controls more than 60 percent of the strip, and intends to continue its occupation indefinitely.
A Gaza security source told AFP there was "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday", as Israeli strikes across Gaza killed three people on Wednesday.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis
Saudi Arabia gathered western partners in Riyadh this week with a request: turn on the weapons spigot to help the kingdom in its war with the Houthis in Yemen, three western officials familiar with the meetings told Middle East Eye.
The sources said that Saudi Arabia is seeking weapons supplies to “deter” Houthi attacks, as it prepares for a drawn-out conflict.
“Saudi Arabia is in the market,” one of the officials told MEE.
Saudi Arabia's search for fresh armaments has also extended to Middle Eastern allies that are part of the Mecca Pact alliance.
A Saudi procurement delegation led by Bandar al-Khorayef, the acting president of the General Authority for Military Industries, visited Turkey last week and met with Haluk Gorgun, the chairman of Turkey’s defence procurement agency. The delegation included representatives from dozens of Saudi companies.
A Turkish official told MEE that Ankara was doing its best to help Riyadh as much as possible by providing equipment as a show of solidarity.
A separate regional official told MEE that Saudi Arabia was looking to acquire anything they could find on the market, including short-range air defence systems effective against drones.
“The Saudis want whatever we have on the shelf,” the person said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Mahmoud Khalil sues US Justice Department over failure to disclose correspondence with immigration judge
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Mahmoud Khalil sues US Justice Department over failure to disclose correspondence with immigration judge
Former Columbia University graduate student Mahmoud Khalil sued the US Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday for its failure to disclose documents showing what correspondence government officials may have had with the immigration judge and the appeal panel in his case.
This follows the administration’s failure to comply with a Freedom of Information Act request Khalil submitted in May, on the heels of a New York Times investigation that revealed his case was expedited and resulted in the recusal of members of the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA).
In April, the BIA issued what it called a "final order of removal" for Khalil, meaning he could be deported from the US. However, he is not permitted to be re-arrested while his free speech case in federal court continues.
The judges who make up the BIA do not operate as an independent judiciary. The BIA falls under the control of the executive branch of government - in this case, the Trump administration. The same applies to all immigration courts, which operate under the purview of the DOJ.
“The Trump administration is determined to deport me to deter others from speaking out for Palestinian liberation, so they rigged the immigration court against me,” Khalil said in a statement on Wednesday from his lawyers at NYU Immigrant Rights Clinic, the Center for Constitutional Rights, and Van Der Hout LLP.
“Now they’re trying to conceal their misconduct. I’m suing to shed light on their lies, corruption, and disgraceful disregard for constitutional rights.”
Khalil had sought records and documents showing what involvement, if any, members of the appeals board, other federal officials, or private actors had in the immigration judge’s decisions.
His case, his lawyers said, was treated "abnormally at every level".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Critics accuse The New York Times of promoting Iran war propaganda
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Critics accuse The New York Times of promoting Iran war propaganda
The New York Times (NYT) is facing widespread criticism over its report claiming that some of Iran's water infrastructure may have been built to support its missile programme, with critics accusing the newspaper of promoting war propaganda and providing a justification for attacks on Iranian civilian infrastructure.
Published on Monday with the headline "War May Answer Longtime Riddle of Iranian Dams Built for No Clear Reason", the article examines the geographical overlap between dam and water infrastructure projects and sites recently struck during the US-Israeli war on Iran. It suggests that some of these projects may have been designed, at least in part, to support military facilities.
One of the two journalists who wrote the piece, Sanam Mahoozi, shared the article on X, writing: “Why has Iran kept building dams amid a severe water crisis? @ErikaSolomon and I examined a striking overlap between water projects and military sites. Could some have served a dual purpose? No conclusive evidence, but questions worth exploring.”
The Iranian Water Diplomacy Association noted on Tuesday "with serious concern" the discrepancies in the report, including the fact that geographical proximity between struck sites and water infrastructure sites does not establish military use.
The report refers to 533 identified dams, but without any statistical analysis, it "has no evidentiary value", the association said. "Historical chronology also does not fit the hypothesis."
"Presenting water infrastructure as military, without credible evidence, blurs the line between civilian objects and military targets in public opinion and normalizes a threat-based view of facilities on which millions depend," the association said in its statement published online.
Read more: Critics accuse The New York Times of promoting Iran war propaganda

Israeli court extends detention of Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safia
Dr Hussam Abu Safia will remain in Israeli detention for at least another six months, after a court extended his detention without bringing any charges against him.
The decision, handed down by a court in Beersheba, came despite mounting concerns over the deteriorating health of the Palestinian doctor, who was seized by Israeli forces in late 2024 after refusing to abandon the Kamal Adwan Hospital he headed in response to Israeli evacuation orders.
Physicians for Human Rights Israel said the court had rejected a request for his release filed by his lawyer.
